scenarios.challenge: A capture-perfect action ages through state evolution while a noisier fresh action remains current.
scenarios.expected_invariant: The time-aware planner may prefer the fresher action even when static planning prefers the capture-perfect action.

scenarios.challenge: Two persistent models assign opposing transition probabilities to the same action.
scenarios.expected_invariant: The robust policy is selected from one shared observable tree and minimizes the maximum complete-mission model risk.

scenarios.challenge: Observation likelihoods are identical across models while transition kernels differ.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Any policy difference is attributable to temporal dynamics uncertainty, not observation likelihood.

scenarios.challenge: Transition kernels are identical across models while observation likelihoods differ.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Any policy difference is attributable to observation-model uncertainty, not state evolution.

scenarios.challenge: A hidden shared-fault regime persists across the mission and affects multiple sensor outcomes.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Repeated observations must update one joint fault posterior; independent multiplication is prohibited.

scenarios.challenge: The mission-persistent model objective is compared with a branchwise model-switching adversary.
scenarios.expected_invariant: The two objectives are reported separately and are not substituted for each other.

scenarios.challenge: No-observation likelihood differs between inside/outside states and the state then evolves.
scenarios.expected_invariant: No-observation conditions the capture belief before model-specific temporal propagation.

scenarios.challenge: A delayed result arrives recently but was captured earlier.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Receipt time does not reset evidence age; use-epoch state is derived from capture time and elapsed age.

scenarios.challenge: Transition evidence or model commitment is absent.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Reject or explicitly mark unknown; never substitute identity transition or certainty.

scenarios.challenge: Evidence age is exactly zero for every model and common-cause regime.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Every zero-age transition must be identity; non-identity input rejects.

scenarios.challenge: A plausible model is added to the persistent candidate set while policy and previous models remain unchanged.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Worst-case risk of a fixed policy cannot decrease when the model set expands.

scenarios.challenge: Persistent model labels are permuted without changing model parameters.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Selected objective value and policy semantics remain invariant under label permutation.

scenarios.challenge: Each observable first-outcome branch selects stop or a second action with different resource costs.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Every reachable branch respects latency, energy and bandwidth ceilings; no action is reused.

scenarios.challenge: The policy input includes a future observation or a future transition/model digest.
scenarios.expected_invariant: Reject chronology leakage; controller decisions use only information available in the observable history.
